instruction: Set the system timezone to UTC+0 and switch the clock to 24-hour format.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Chains the original UTC+0 timezone goal with a second objective: enabling 24-hour clock display in GNOME Date & Time settings. The custom getter runs `date +%z` and `gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface clock-format`; the metric awards 0.5 for each sub-goal. Initial state (HKT timezone, default 12h clock) scores 0.0.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened GNOME Settings > Date & Time, clicked the Time Zone row, searched for 'Reykjavik', selected it (UTC+0/GMT), and closed the dialog.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate GNOME Settings > Date & Time panel, interact with the timezone picker, and toggle display options.
metadata.task_rationale: Compositional hardening: chains the proven timezone-change capability with an additional time format toggle in the same Date & Time settings panel.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts both required states: timezone offset via `date +%z` and GNOME clock format via `gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface clock-format`.
Metric covers both instruction requirements: UTC+0 timezone (checks offset == '+0000') and 24-hour clock format (checks clock_format == '24h' after stripping quotes).
Partial credit scoring (0.5 each) is semantically appropriate for this two-objective task.
gsettings output quote-stripping logic (.strip("'\"")) correctly handles the single-quoted output format.
No postconfig needed since verification uses shell commands (`date`, `gsettings`) rather than UI state inspection.
Negative-control resistant: initial state (HKT/+0800 timezone, 12h clock) would score 0.0.
Minor: `expected` parameter from rules dict is unused (hardcoded comparison values), but hardcoded values match the declared rules exactly so there is no functional discrepancy.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Optional improvement: use `expected.get('expected_offset', '+0000')` and `expected.get('expected_clock', '24h')` in the metric to make it data-driven rather than hardcoded, improving maintainability.
